components.name: Primary Button

components.css: .ds-ledger { display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(0,1.2fr) minmax(480px,.8fr); overflow: hidden; border-top: 3px solid #9a7932; border-radius: 8px; background: #fff; color: #17202b; box-shadow: 0 8px 22px rgba(13,31,49,.08); transition: box-shadow 150ms cubic-bezier(0.33,0,0.67,1); } .ds-ledger:hover { box-shadow: 0 8px 24px rgba(13,31,49,.10); } .ds-ledger:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #c7b27d; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-ledger-identity { display: grid; align-content: center; gap: 8px; padding: 26px 28px; } .ds-ledger-title-row { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; flex-wrap: wrap; } .ds-ledger-title { margin: 0; color: #0b223b; font: 600 24px/32px "Source Serif 4", Georgia, serif; letter-spacing: -.02em; } .ds-ledger-stage { padding: 2px 6px; border-radius: 3px; background: #e8edf2; color: #0b223b; font: 700 10px/14px Aptos, "Segoe UI", Calibri, Arial, sans-serif; letter-spacing: .06em; } .ds-ledger-copy { margin: 0; max-width: 72ch; color: #495463; font: 400 14px/20px Aptos, "Segoe UI", Calibri, Arial, sans-serif; } .ds-ledger-metrics { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(4,minmax(0,1fr)); border-left: 1px solid #dedbd2; background: #f5f3ee; } .ds-ledger-metric { display: grid; align-content: center; gap: 5px; min-height: 92px; padding: 18px 16px; border-right: 1px solid #dedbd2; } .ds-ledger-metric:last-child { border-right: 0; } .ds-ledger-metric strong { color: #0b223b; font: 600 24px/1 Aptos, "Segoe UI", Calibri, Arial, sans-serif; } .ds-ledger-metric span { color: #66717e; font: 600 11px/1.35 Aptos, "Segoe UI", Calibri, Arial, sans-serif; letter-spacing: .08em; text-transform: uppercase; } @media (max-width: 1050px) { .ds-ledger { grid-template-columns: 1fr; } .ds-ledger-metrics { border-top: 1px solid #dedbd2; border-left: 0; } } @media (max-width: 620px) { .ds-ledger-metrics { grid-template-columns: repeat(2,minmax(0,1fr)); } }

narrative.overview:
The interface is a formal operating ledger rather than generic SaaS chrome. Deep navy architecture establishes institutional continuity; antique-gold rules mark authority sparingly; warm paper surfaces hold dense evidence, review, lineage, and assurance data with the calm precision of a committee book.

Brand expression remains concentrated in the supplied Stratton emblem and wordmark, the persistent rail, serif headings, and exact rules. The working field is deliberately restrained so decision-critical state, provenance, human authority, and fail-closed conditions remain immediately legible across desktop, tablet, and mobile layouts.
keyCharacteristics: Deep navy institutional architecture with antique-gold authority marks.
Warm paper surfaces separated by precise rules and low, structural shadows.
Source Serif 4 headings paired with compact Aptos/Segoe UI operational text.
A persistent desktop rail that becomes horizontal workflow navigation at tablet widths.
A case ledger summary that preserves mandate and workflow context above every workspace.
Restrained semantic status tints with explicit non-color labels.

rules.name: The Ledger, Not Dashboard Rule
rules.body: Compose screens as ordered records, evidence tables, review controls, and committee preparation—not decorative analytics.

rules.name: The Authority-Mark Rule
rules.body: Antique gold marks institutional authority and focus; it is never a broad decorative fill.

rules.name: The Status-Is-Evidence Rule
rules.body: Semantic colors always travel with an explicit text label, never as color-only meaning.

rules.name: The Serif-for-Authority Rule
rules.body: Use Source Serif 4 for headings that establish mandate, place, or decision context; keep controls and operational data in the body sans serif.

rules.name: The Compact-Data Rule
rules.body: Use small uppercase labels only for status, metric, and navigation metadata—not for paragraph copy.

rules.name: The Persistent Context Rule
rules.body: The mandate, active workspace, case identity, and ledger summary remain visible before task-specific content.

rules.name: The Controlled Collapse Rule
rules.body: Tablet and mobile layouts preserve workflow order and labels; they change orientation rather than removing decision context.

rules.name: The Structural-Depth Rule
rules.body: Use rules and tonal paper changes first; reserve shadows for hierarchy, stickiness, or explicit containment.

rules.name: The Reserved-Curve Rule
rules.body: Rounded forms support touch and grouping but never make the ledger feel playful or pill-heavy.

dos: Do keep the deep navy rail, command context, and case ledger as the persistent institutional frame.
Do use antique gold only for authority rules, focus, and restrained brand strokes.
Do set mandate, workspace, case, and major section headings in Source Serif 4.
Do keep operational data compact, ordered, and separated by exact rules.
Do preserve explicit text labels for every semantic status.
Do retain the supplied Stratton emblem and wordmark as the canonical brand assets.
donts: Don't replace the ledger hierarchy with generic dashboard tiles, decorative charts, or consumer SaaS chrome.
Don't use gold as a large background, gradient, or decorative accent field.
Don't make semantic status color louder than the evidence or decision content it qualifies.
Don't introduce oversized type, excessive whitespace, or rounded pill surfaces that reduce operational density.
Don't hide mandate, case, workflow, provenance, or human-authority context during responsive collapse.
Don't imply automated investment approval; committee submission remains visibly human-only and unavailable.
